_comment: STAGE-D per-unit coverage registry for the full-coverage program
(docs/twin_validation/wave2_6_unit_test_contract.md SS12.3/12.4; work-list
docs/twin_validation/l3_release_package_unit_inventory.md). This is the GENERAL,
registry-DRIVEN successor to the Wave-2.6 pilot registry: the audit reads its
canonical set, its covered_by test-file set, and its reconcile-module list FROM this
file (the Wave-2.6 script's hard-coded 19-unit tuple is the pilot-only fallback).
Audited by outputs/twin_validation/wave2_6_coverage_audit.py --registry <this file>
(runner outputs/twin_validation/stage_d_coverage_run.sh). Batches accumulate here
D1..D20; each adds its module's CPU-pure units + reconcile entry.
SCHEMA (superset of the pilot registry -- same AST-derived, anti-stale core):
* default_target: per-unit statement+branch floor (default 100%/100%).
* covered_by_test_files: the files a bare covered_by name may resolve in.
* reconcile_modules: for each listed source module the audit enumerates EVERY
public unit from the AST (top-level public def + public method of a public class,
incl. __post_init__) and requires each to be either a registered unit's qualname
OR listed in out_of_scope -- the AST-derived anti-under-population guard (stronger
than the pilot's hard-coded list: it cannot drift).
* out_of_scope: {qualname: reason} for public units intentionally NOT L0/L1-scored
in this batch (GPU/quimb-bound tail -> Tier-4 lighter treatment; retracted units).
* canonical_units: the exact set of registered unit labels (units[] must be a
bijection with this list -- a missing OR stray unit is a hard audit error).
* units[]: {group, module, unit, qualname, target, exemptions[]}. Exemptions are
DATA with STABLE selectors, each carrying a non-empty covered_by that must EXIST.
D1 -- quantum_bath/observables.py (7 CPU-pure units, was 0% direct). One DEFENSIVE
BRANCH: exact_cmi_bits `if den>0 and num>0` False arc is structurally unreachable for
any dict (recomputed marginals dominate: P12,P23,P2 >= p>0 whenever p>0), so it is a
dead log2-guard, not a trippable assert. Registered as a line/branch exemption whose
covered_by is the invariant proof test_cmi_guard_invariant_den_num_positive_when_p_positive.

units.note: NO exemption (review finding 2 correction). The `if den>0 and num>0` guard's False arc is NOT dead: a valid non-negative normalized distribution with a tiny term (e.g. {(0,0,0):1e-200,(1,1,1):1-1e-200}) underflows num=p*P2 to exactly 0.0, so the False arc IS reachable and is covered honestly by test_L0_exact_cmi_bits_underflow_reaches_guard_false_arc. The guard does real work (returns 0.0 for that term instead of log2(0/0)=nan) -- it is a live underflow/validity guard, not defensive dead code.
